description: A hillside that stood up. Moss and granite shift when it breathes, and climbers swear the mountain growled.
lore: Every valley had its one hill, and the people in it agreed on that hill's shape the way they agreed on almost nothing else: the same dark line against the same evening, seen from the same doorway, for generation after generation. And every hill of that kind carried the same story — there is a bear up there, do not go up after dark, I mean it. A hundred valleys' worth of that, held identically by everybody who ever lived in sight of one, and it does not stay a hill. The story stood up and brought the hill with it.

Moving costs it. The seams open green down its legs when it walks and the moss tears along the shoulders, so mostly it declines to, and holds one position for years while people treat it as exactly what it looks like. There was a rota fire on the western rounds kept in its lee for eleven winters — out of the weather, with a wall at your back you could lean on all night. One spring the wall left. The keeper lost the fire twice to the wind before morning and finished the shift anyway, talking to whoever came, in the open, with nothing behind her. [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] has a private word for keepers who do that. She has never once said it to their faces. The wall is somewhere further west now, standing still again, with eleven winters of soot up one flank.
gm_notes: Made: the raw material is the shape of a landmark plus the warning story attached to it — the most identically-remembered thing a valley has. The turn is the fire that lost its shelter; Solveig appears sideways (as the person who notices such keepers) rather than in a scene, to avoid repeating her white_rabbit vigil. Soot on the flank is the reusable hook: a Cragback can be identified by what was burned against it.
